There appears to be a survivor who's escaped punishment at the Desert Pavilion...

#### Explore the Desert Pavilion

#### Explore the Desert Pavilion

#### Trace the voice

#### Talk to the person asking for help

**???:** You people... I've not seen you around before. Are there really still newcomers showing up now?

**Venipi:** But since Dex is with you, I suppose you're backup. My name is Venipi, and I come from an era when King Deshret's divine form still walked among us.

**Paimon:** Paimon's the name, and this is Traveler. And our team's got one more member, Zeitlind.

**Paimon:** We're probably what you consider people from the most recent era.

**Venipi:** Zeitlind... Would you happen to have an older sister, by any chance?

**Zeitlind:** Do you know my sister too?

**Venipi:** Of course. Here, everyone is friends with everyone. It matters little what station they occupied in their former life.

**Venipi:** In my day, I was a nobody, just one of many working on King Deshret's mausoleum.

**Venipi:** I was traveling in the desert one day when I was suddenly plucked from the sands and thrown into the Apathic Interval, where I was for... I want to say less than a hundred years?

**Venipi:** Then, once I left and came here, I found the place full of ancients, some from times preceding even King Deshret himself. But we all got along just the same.

**Venipi:** Later on, the sisters of the deity here told me they hadn't plucked any desert buildings, and asked that I reconstruct them from memory.

**Venipi:** It was only with everyone's help that we managed to build this place at all. But now... look at these ruins.

**Paimon:** You know, speaking of which, Paimon has a question. Those sand statues out there... are those, um... artworks from your era? You know, from back in King Deshret's day?

**Zeitlind:** Perhaps they were created to serve as a reminder of the impermanence of the physical body and life itself...?

**Venipi:** ...You truly are different from your sister. You must really enjoy reading, like the others.

**Venipi:** Those are people — all of them. They were punished by being turned into sand.

**Paimon:** Whoa!

**Venipi:** Don't worry, they're all still alive. Death does not exist here. They'll be restored once the problem here is resolved.

**Paimon:** Oh, wait — didn't you say that whoever saved you would get that coin King Deshret gave you as a reward?

**Paimon:** Paimon bets it's worth a lot of Mora!

**Venipi:** Haha, I'm not handing it over! It's my lucky charm! Besides, it's the only thing I have left to remind me of my old life.

**Paimon:** Pfft. Since it's so important to you... Alright, guess we'll be super nice and not press you for payment.

**Venipi:** Ugh, we've been chatting for too long! Looks like it's here!

**Venipi:** We don't have time to stand around talking. Are you at least at the level of a novice Remurian Centurion?

**Paimon:** There we go again! Paimon doesn't even know what kind of standard this is supposed to be...

#### Defeat the Keepers

#### Talk to Venipi

**Venipi:** Oof, that was quite something. You're easily at the level of a high-ranking Centurion!

- **Traveler:** Didn't you have your own hierarchy back in King Deshret's day?

**Venipi:** Well, those scholars at the Mahavaipulya Archives have read enough books that their combat assessments actually hold some weight.

**Venipi:** Ah, it's nice to be so well read.

**Venipi:** For instance...

**Venipi:** On average, the knights serving under Erinnyes could take on three standard Remurian Centurions at once, though they're half a rank below Erinnyes.

**Venipi:** Medjay, who served the Crocodile King, wasn't considered exactly an elite fighter, but was highly adept at dealing with monsters. So in terms of rough power level...

**Paimon:** Alright, alright, let's go save your friends first!

- **Traveler:** But I wanna know more.

**Paimon:** We can talk about that later!

#### Defeat the Keepers

#### Look for Vitruvius

**Vitruvius:** Venipi! You're still alive! How wonderful to see you!

**Vitruvius:** Of course I know that death is not possible here. What I mean is, I'm so glad you didn't turn into sand.

**Vitruvius:** Anyway, you know what I mean.

**Venipi:** I do.

**Vitruvius:** And thanks to all of you, and Dex too.

**Zeitlind:** I didn't do a thing.

Venipi introduces you all to Vitruvius and recounts what just happened...

**Vitruvius:** Incredible — your strength exceeds even that of a typical Chief Centurion!

**Paimon:** Now, even Paimon's kinda interested to see how you actually stack up in that system.

- **Traveler:** Oh yeah?

**Vitruvius:** In that case, I'll take you to the others.

**Vitruvius:** After all, Venipi only provided the pattern work and motifs from King Deshret's times. I was the one responsible for the main layout and pathways in this area.

**Venipi:** That's right. While this may look like a building from some gilded age, it's really the result of everyone's knowledge.

#### Follow Vitruvius

#### Follow Vitruvius

**Vitruvius:** Don't come any closer!

**Vitruvius:** It might be a bit self-indulgent to worry about my own epitaph. You probably think me ridiculous, but I've actually already decided what mine will be.

**Vitruvius:** "Please, tell my love in Patraipolis that——"

**Paimon:** Vitruvius!

**Zeitlind:** ...He turned into sand even before he was done speaking.

**Venipi:** Ah, I'm hopeless — I'm actually fighting the urge to chuckle out loud at this sad juncture. He's going to be so mortified once he stops being sand.

**Zeitlind:** That's a rather optimistic take on the situation.

**Venipi:** We have a choice to make. Do we deal with that guard first? Or search for survivors for as long as we can?

#### Talk to the survivor(s)

**Kshama:** Venipi! Dex! And Raumhilda and our new friends! Thank you all!

**Zeitlind:** ...I'm her younger sister Zeitlind.

**Kshama:** I see. The two of you look so much alike, and oh so pretty. My name is Kshama, and I come from... Ah, what was I going to say?

**Kshama:** I see. The two of you look so much alike, and oh so pretty. My name is Kshama, and I come from Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's era.

**Kshama:** The era in which the Dendro Archon had yet to become a child.

Venipi introduces Kshama, and Vitruvius's tragic circumstances are revealed...

They also speak of the epitaph he took thousands of years to come up with.

**Kshama:** That is beyond absurd.

**Venipi:** If I hadn't told you, you would never have known.

**Kshama:** Now that you have, it's going to be hard for me to look Vitruvius in the eye without laughing.

**Venipi:** Alright, enough small talk. We've come all this way, and it doesn't look like we've missed anything.

**Venipi:** Is there anyone else?

**Kshama:** I'm afraid not.

**Venipi:** Then how about how we can stop folks from turning into sand? Any ideas?

**Kshama:** We didn't manage to learn much from exploring earlier. After all, no one here at the Desert Pavilion is well-versed in the mystic arts or the sciences.

**Kshama:** So, it seems we're back to the only known method: defeating the Punisher of Gomorrah.

**Venipi:** That you need not worry about. We have Traveler, who has the strength of a Remurian Tribune.

**Zeitlind:** Looks like someone's been promoted again.

**Kshama:** But there's no way to find the Punisher of Gomorrah. It has hidden its form.

**Venipi:** That is a problem, yes.

**Paimon:** You know, it wasn't easy getting everyone out. How about we leave this place first and get back to the main hall?

**Paimon:** Istoria and Josephus are there too. They seem rather knowledgeable, so maybe they know a way.

**Kshama:** Oh, Istoria's safe too? That's really good to know. He's the most experienced of us all, and is always open to learning new things.

**Kshama:** If we're talking about anecdotes, history, and culture, he's probably the most knowledgeable person in this world.

**Venipi:** Then let's go now. The earlier we get back, the earlier we can figure this out and save Vitruvius and the rest!

**Vitruvius:** That's right, it's all over, and everyone's been restored.

**Kshama:** ...

**Venipi:** Fine, fine. No more laughing.

**Paimon:** Oh, where's Zeitlind, by the way?

**Vitruvius:** I've no idea. I was standing outside with everyone else. They were still in each other's arms a moment ago.

**Vitruvius:** I told little Scarpa to stop and get everyone back to the main hall. Then I left them and came over to you.

**Vitruvius:** Everyone should still be somewhere around here. In which case, she can't have gone very far yet.

**Zeitlind:** This is...

**Paimon:** ...An amethyst brooch.

**Zeitlind:** It belongs to my older sister, and was one of the things in my suitcase that I lost.

**Paimon:** Ah, got it now! Nice, that's one taken care of.

**Venipi:** It must have been placed here as an exhibit from this era.

**Vitruvius:** Actually, the reason I started thinking about what to write on my epitaph is because your sister asked about it. Those words weren't exactly things I've been holding in for thousands of years.

**Raumhilda:** Does nobody die here? Wouldn't it be impossible for anyone to leave behind a truly magnificent epitaph then?

**Vitruvius:** Given my former status, I could probably be laid to rest at the priests' cemetery, alongside branches of silver and white.

**Vitruvius:** Which would be a tremendous honor, albeit one without any space for an epitaph.

**Raumhilda:** In that case, it's a no for me. Because I've already written mine.

**Raumhilda:** And it says——

**Venipi:** Thank you so much.

**Paimon:** And what about that coin of yours? The one from King Deshret's day?

**Venipi:** You're still thinking about that? Fine, you can have it once I've finished chanting my ten thousand prayers of penance to King Deshret.

**Vitruvius:** This one over here got worked up upon hearing Kshama talk about the King's fall that he actually cried, "You lie! You lie!"

**Vitruvius:** "You lied! Liar! That's impossible!"

**Vitruvius:** Honestly, that's better for a laugh than my epitaph.

**Paimon:** Eh, if you're gonna be so grudging with the coin, just forget it.

**Paimon:** Hmph. And this is the point where we say we're only here to help Zeitlind find what she lost.

**Paimon:** We're helping you out just 'cause you happened to be here!

**Zeitlind:** ...Thank you, Paimon. Thank you, Traveler.

**Paimon:** Oh, no, no. You only got dragged into this because of us. So, we gotta make this right for you.

**Venipi:** Such undisguised partiality.

**Zeitlind:** I'm truly grateful to you two.

#### Leave the Desert Pavilion

**Paimon:** Oh, you're here, Istoria!

**Istoria:** Indeed. Everyone from the Desert Pavilion is now back at the main hall, which is why I hurried over here.

**Istoria:** Zeitlind, have you found what you were looking for?

**Zeitlind:** Yes, I have. Thanks for asking.

**Istoria:** Splendid.

**Istoria:** By the way, do you know what the names "Melanta" and "Nihilita" mean?

**Paimon:** Paimon will go first! Nope!

**Zeitlind:** Yes. They mean "melancholy" and "nothingness," don't they?

**Istoria:** Most sagacious of you! I believe you and I shall be even better friends than I was with your sister, since we have the same interests.

**Zeitlind:** Yes, my sister's the outdoorsy, extroverted type. Still, before I could read for myself, she used to read to me all the time.

**Istoria:** Yet, what has "melancholy" got to do with someone like that?

**Istoria:** Of course, I speak of pathological melancholy, not the sort The One above feels when gazing upon on our suffering.

**Zeitlind:** ...Did she tell you all that?

**Istoria:** Frankly, I was agape at the revelations she presented. I wouldn't have thought anyone audacious enough to build a sanatorium atop the site from which the Temple of Space had ascended.

**Istoria:** Did you know? It was initially thought that melancholy was a biological ailment. The word itself actually comes from the term for "black bile."

**Istoria:** But subsequently, people came to believe that melancholy was an affliction of the heart.

**Paimon:** Well, it does take time to get to the right answer...

**Istoria:** But today, humans have once again discovered the truth: melancholy is indeed also pathological. Thus, both medication and companionship are vital to recovery.

**Istoria:** We already knew all that back in my day. The angels had told us so.

**Istoria:** But while the songs of the angels and the latter-day Anemo Archon can cure melancholy, the hollow consolations of ordinary folk cannot be expected to work such wonders.

**Zeitlind:** What are you trying to say?

**Istoria:** I shall to have to whisper this, for it is a secret.

**Istoria:** Why would the great One above who rules over sky and space name her own creations "nothingness" and "melancholy"?

**Istoria:** They say she lacks the ability to empathize with others. There is nothing she cannot do, yet she is utterly helpless against genuine futility and the ailments of the human heart.

**Istoria:** This is why she named her creations the two things she is least able to deal with.

**Paimon:** Paimon gets that. Naming things after enemies you've never beaten makes them sound cool and powerful.

**Paimon:** Paimon's would be called "No Mora," "Hunger," and "No Traveler."

- **Traveler:** Heh. They sound weak.

**Zeitlind:** I fear I can't keep up with your thousand year's worth of wisdom.

**Istoria:** Hahaha! Wisdom? Bah.

**Istoria:** I pray for the courage to give this all up and live a real life once more. Can you see what I'm saying?

**Istoria:** Feel free to come to me if you ever need anything — even if all you want is to talk about your sister.

**Zeitlind:** I... will do that.

#### Talk to the rescued

**Daozi:** Reach out your hand and touch the painting. Break this veil of illusion, and the world beyond shall receive you once more.

**Paimon:** Huh? What are you talking about?

**Daozi:** In simpler terms, touch the painting, and you'll be able to return. Though the world outside is just another illusion.

**Daozi:** Hahaha! Mountains cannot crush the buried spirit; through riven clouds, the sky at last appears. I'm free!

**Daozi:** Hilda, Dex, and my new friends, please, accept my thanks.

**Zeitlind:** I'm her younger sister, Zeitlind.

**Daozi:** Oh? Why, you two look so alike!

**Zeitlind:** Yes, I've been told that a lot.

**Daozi:** And who are these two?

**Paimon:** My name's Paimon! And this is Traveler. It was Istoria's commission that brought us here.

**Daozi:** In that case, let's dispense with the introductions. Do you possess any degree of martial skill? Preferably of the sort that might see off a Legatus of Remuria.

**Paimon:** Just how did you come up with that description?

**Daozi:** Ah, this goes back to how a certain border fortress rose to prominence when Remuria was destroyed.

**Daozi:** One day, after much time had passed, an old man arrived at its gates, claiming to be the acting master of the Guhua Clan.

**Daozi:** One day, the two sides fell to arguing.

**Daozi:** When the Remurian commander said that he was in charge of music in the army, the acting master thought him weak.

**Daozi:** But in truth, the greater your musical mastery, the higher your rank in the Remurian military. And this commander, why, he had already undergone petrification!

**Daozi:** By the way, I don't know if you've heard of this, but everyone in the Remurian inner circles was transformed into "Ichor," becoming semi-immortal golems.

**Daozi:** So, when the acting master channeled his inner energies into a single strike, he only wound up hurting his own hand.

**Paimon:** Uhhh...

**Daozi:** He then spoke harshly, lamenting a lack of successors to the Guhua Clan's secret arts and the withering of talent on the vine in his era. Why, so he claimed, he didn't even possess a Vision!

**Daozi:** — Of course, he wouldn't have been selected if he had one in the first place.

**Daozi:** After enduring the Apathic Interval, we could no longer receive Visions... But anyway, back to our story.

**Daozi:** The commander shot back with choice words of his own, claiming that the Legati of Remuria were far more terrifying than he could ever be.

**Paimon:** Eh, sure. Cool story, Paimon supposes? Also, don't worry. Traveler's one thousand percent got what it takes to defeat a Legatus.

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** With both hands tied behind my back, even!

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Best that I keep a low profile, eh?

##### Shared continuation

**Daozi:** Hahaha, that's great.

**Paimon:** By the way, why were you in the painting? And what are those humanoid ink blots?

**Daozi:** This is how Melanta delivers punishment: Sealing people into paintings and smushing them into ink blots.

**Daozi:** Just like my cage, which was encased in layers of paintings.

**Paimon:** So the ink blots we saw back there were actually... people?

**Daozi:** Yes.

**Daozi:** Now, a word to the wise.

**Daozi:** The more realistic a painting is, the more fitting a cage it is to ensconce your spirit. After all, its essence may be grasped at a glance.

**Daozi:** As such, expect hidden secrets lurking behind any realistic paintings you find here.

**Paimon:** And what should we do next?

**Daozi:** This is not the right place for such talk. Let's head back first.

#### Investigate the painting

#### Talk to your companions

**Paimon:** Huh. We sure made it back quickly!

**Zeitlind:** This place truly is full of wonders.

**Daozi:** It is indeed fabulous, comparable to the finishing touch from Rex Lapis's hand, which brought stone to life.

**Daozi:** And with the power of your heart and mind, you can really turn those lifelike paintings into reality.

**Paimon:** Anyway, what's our next plan of action?

**Daozi:** The key to restoring the entire library lies in completing that final, illuminating stroke. But before we do that, we must first restore this painting.

**Daozi:** "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White."

**Paimon:** Wh—What a commanding name.

**Daozi:** That's Inazuman preferences in painting names for you.

**Daozi:** Theoretically, we should be able to complete the missing part of the painting in the Tower of Radiant Light.

**Daozi:** But with our path barred, it seems we can only head to the Abode of Resplendent Talent to see if we can reach the Tower of Radiant Light from there.

**Paimon:** Wait, it was behind this door the whole time?

**Paimon:** Paimon had Traveler kick this thing, full force! Traveler's strong enough to level mountains, but the door didn't even budge.

**Daozi:** Is your foot numb?

- **Traveler:** Yeah...

**Daozi:** Probably because this door was manifested from the painting through the mind. As such, it doesn't exist as physical matter as we know it.

**Daozi:** Istoria once mentioned that he had a teacher named Aristocles, who was always saying that "mind prevails over matter." I guess this is what they meant.

**Daozi:** But leveling mountains, you say... That would make you just as powerful as Azhdaha. Speaking of which...

**Daozi:** Yu Huangyi from the Mahavaipulya Chamber told me that Azhdaha already existed back in his era.

**Daozi:** As such, the so-called "finishing touch" that brought the dragon to life was nothing more than a legend, the invention of later generations. A fine story all the same, of course.

**Paimon:** And did you realize something from that?

**Daozi:** I just told him, "You've ruined a precious memory, you know that?"

**Zeitlind:** I can relate.

**Daozi:** *sigh* Never mind, just take it as a fun little anecdote. Anyway, since the door was born from a painting, a painter must open it. Allow me to do that for you.

**Zeitlind:** You don't seem very surprised.

**Paimon:** That's because Traveler's been through even crazier stuff.

**Zeitlind:** Lots of extraordinary adventures, huh? Guess I shouldn't even be surprised if you've saved the world before.

**Paimon:** He and his sister were separated by an awful god. / She and her brother were separated by an awful god.

**Paimon:** The main goal of our adventure is to find his lost sibling. / The main goal of our adventure is to find her lost sibling.

**Paimon:** So Traveler can understand how you feel.

**Zeitlind:** I hope you find your sibling, and may you live a life of peace and happiness.

**Paimon:** Oh... Paimon's sorry. She forgot that you won't...

**Zeitlind:** Ah, please, don't apologize. It was my fault for bringing it up. Also, that's not what I meant.

**Zeitlind:** I really hope that your wish comes true.

- **Traveler:** Thank you, Zeitlind.

**Daozi:** Alright. Open sesame!

**Paimon:** Let's get moving, then!

#### Head to the Abode of Resplendent Talent

#### Investigate the room

#### Talk to your companions

**Zeitlind:** These photos...

**Daozi:** Ah, they were painted using a Kamera, yes?

**Daozi:** Back then, your sister told us of something capable of creating pictures even more lifelike than the most realistic paintings.

**Daozi:** We all wondered what it would be like.

**Daozi:** It's a shame that she didn't have a Kamera, nor did she have a picture painted by it on hand.

**Daozi:** Now that I've seen one myself, it does look incredibly lifelike.

**Paimon:** Hehe, how's that for feeling smug? Machines have taken realism to its natural end, but there's still room for imagination, y'know?

**Daozi:** Not exactly. No matter how realistic the painting, it still carries the painter's emotions and aesthetic sense.

**Daozi:** Though some of the colors can't be found in the real world, you can really feel the painter's heart from the way said colors are used.

**Daozi:** Even the most realistic painting carries within it minor details of fiction, exaggeration, and blur. That's where the artist's aesthetics and craft come into play.

**Paimon:** Okay... It's not like Paimon doesn't get it. Paimon just wanted to compliment you so she could ask you to, y'know, maybe draw something for us later...?

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** Don't you already have Albedo's painting of you?

**Paimon:** Paimon wants to see what a more expressive version of her would look like, though!

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Could we take it with us?

**Daozi:** I don't think you could take it with you. Otherwise, you'd make a lot of Mora from selling my paintings.

**Paimon:** Lots of Mora, huh? Were you a famous painter or something?

**Daozi:** "Let me have a look. Hmm, I can't believe I'm looking at an authentic Yunlai Daoxuan! And painted just last week, too!"

##### Shared continuation

**Zeitlind:** Thank you so much.

**Paimon:** Zeitlind, could Paimon have a look?

**Zeitlind:** Sure. These photos were taken during my sister's vacation.

**Zeitlind:** The passerby she asked was really bad at photography, so some photos only show the top of her head poking out from the bottom.

**Daozi:** But I can tell that she's smiling happily all the same.

**Zeitlind:** Sorry to let you see that. The lighting and composition of these photos are terrible. There's no sense of depth or layering at all.

**Daozi:** It's not that bad. I think these are the best... uh, pho-toes.

**Daozi:** If your sister hadn't insisted on only showing her head, these would've been the worst of scenic paintings... I mean, scenic photos.
